newsitem.title: CHINA: China says "one country, two systems" suits Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China says "one country, two systems" suits Taiwan.

text.p: Chinese Premier Li Peng hailed the resumption of sovereignty over Hong Kong as a new era for the region and said on Tuesday a similar recovery formula could ensure reunification with rival Taiwan.
"The 'one country, two systems' formula works for Hong Kong and Macau," Li told a reception in Beijing. "It can also work for Taiwan.

It was the first time since Beijing resumed sovereignty over Hong Kong at midnight on Monday that China had so explicitly suggested to Taiwan, which it regards as a renegade province, that it should follow Hong Kong's example. Taiwan has rejected this formula, insisting on reunification under a democratic system.

"No matter how many difficulties we meet on the road ahead, we must certainly realise complete reunification of the motherland," Li told the reception in the Great Hall of the People. "It can also certainly be realised."
"This is not only to celebrate the start of a new era for Hong Kong, it is also to celebrate a major victory in the peaceful reunification of China," Li said.
Macau, a Portuguese-run enclave about 40 km (25 miles) west of Hong Kong, reverts to Chinese administration in 1999.
